summary: Fixes profile-picture upload for users with no picture (settings form skips old-image deletion when empty; removeUserOldImageFromCDN takes the URL from the client); renames Prisma client db->prisma; moves getUserSubscriptionPlan into a 'use server' file; uploadthing updates.

statements.text: ⚠ Anyone may be able to use the 'remove user old image from cdn' action to delete files from your storage: no login check. Add one and restrict to allowed files.
statements.why: settings/actions.ts server action has no session/ownership check and deletes the caller-supplied UploadThing URL.

statements.text: ⚠ Anyone can use the 'get user subscription plan' action without logging in.
statements.why: 'use server' exposes getUserSubscriptionPlan(userId) with no session check; returns Stripe ids/period end.

statements.text: • The dashboard billing page changed in a way plain can't describe yet.
statements.why: Only import path changed; true but uninformative.

statements.text: + getUserSubscriptionPlan() moved into a 'use server' file so the browser can call it directly. It looks up users.
statements.why: Helper moved from lib/subscription.ts to actions/subscription.ts with 'use server'.

statements.text: • The stripe part of your server changed in a way plain can't describe yet. This is the code that charges your customers. Make a test payment before you ship.
statements.why: Only import changed; harmless advice, nothing payment-related changed.

statements.text: • The agent changed the auth login github callback, send OTP, verify OTP, uploadthing, webhooks stripe, generate email verification code, verify verification code, project actions, update user and remove user old image from cdn in ways plain can't describe yet.
statements.why: Lumps a pure db->prisma rename with the two real behaviour changes (client-supplied image URL; skip deletion when no picture) without describing either.

statements.text: • The agent also changed settings-form.tsx, uploadthing/core.ts and pricing.tsx, in ways plain can't describe yet.
statements.why: settings-form has the real fix; uploadthing and pricing changed.

misses.what: The actual fix: users without a profile picture (e.g. email-OTP sign-ups) can now upload an avatar and save settings; previously saving failed.
updateUser(id, payload) in the settings actions is still an unauthenticated server action that updates any user's name/email/picture (pre-existing).
